info.title: OnDemand Spatial earthquake_search
info.description: Search recent/historical earthquakes from the USGS FDSN Event Web Service by time window, magnitude range and geographic area (circle or bounding box), proxied by the OnDemand Spatial serverless route `api/[...route].js` -> `server/serverless/earthquakes-route.js` -> `server/sources/usgs-earthquakes.js`. Returns observed events with UTC time, magnitude, depth, location, tsunami flag and USGS URL. No authentication is required.

servers.description: OnDemand Spatial deployment host — REPLACE with the READY Vercel preview URL or project domain before importing (see x-ondemand-spatial.deployment); the sandbox emulator host is ephemeral

get.description: All query parameters are optional and are forwarded to the USGS FDSN Event Web Service `query` (or `count`) method after validation. A circle search (`latitude` + `longitude` + `maxradiuskm`) and a bounding-box search (`minlatitude`/`maxlatitude`/`minlongitude`/`maxlongitude`) are mutually exclusive -- supplying keys from both is a 400 error, and a partial circle (e.g. `latitude` without `maxradiuskm`) is also a 400 error. Any query parameter not listed below is rejected with 400 (`additionalProperties: false` on the underlying input schema).

parameters.name: starttime
parameters.description: Limit to events on or after this time (UTC). Accepts `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS(Z)`; a date with no time means midnight UTC.

parameters.name: endtime
parameters.description: Limit to events on or before this time (UTC). Same accepted formats as `starttime`.

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description: Circle-search center latitude, degrees. Requires `longitude` and `maxradiuskm` together.

parameters.name: longitude
parameters.description: Circle-search center longitude, degrees. Requires `latitude` and `maxradiuskm` together.

parameters.name: maxradiuskm
parameters.description: Circle-search radius, kilometers (max is USGS's own limit, half the Earth's circumference). Requires `latitude` and `longitude` together.

parameters.name: minlatitude
parameters.description: Bounding-box south edge, degrees. Must be <= `maxlatitude`.

parameters.name: maxlatitude
parameters.description: Bounding-box north edge, degrees. Must be >= `minlatitude`.

parameters.name: minlongitude
parameters.description: Bounding-box west edge, degrees. Must be <= `maxlongitude`.

parameters.name: maxlongitude
parameters.description: Bounding-box east edge, degrees. Must be >= `minlongitude`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return. USGS itself allows up to 20000; this adapter caps it at 200. Defaults to 100.

parameters.name: orderby
parameters.description: Sort order for the returned events.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Local switch (not forwarded to USGS): 'query' returns matching events, 'count' returns only the number of matching events (uses the FDSN `count` endpoint).

200.description: Matching earthquakes (mode=query, the default), or their count only (mode=count -- in which case `events` is omitted and `count` alone reflects the number of matching events).

400.description: Invalid query -- an unknown parameter, an out-of-range or malformed value, a mixed circle/bbox request, a partial circle, or an inverted bounding box. Also carries a USGS-rejected request (HTTP 400) passed through unchanged from the upstream FDSN service.

502.description: Upstream error: USGS was unreachable or timed out after one retry, USGS returned a 5xx or a response body that was not valid JSON, or an unhandled exception occurred in the route handler. (The live route may occasionally surface this same failure under a different HTTP status, e.g. 404/500/503/504, depending on how USGS itself responded -- see server/sources/usgs-earthquakes.js `requestUsgs()`; this document models every such upstream failure uniformly under 502 per this schema's scope.)

EarthquakeSearchResponse.description: Success body for mode=query (default). For mode=count, `events` is omitted and `count` alone reflects the number of matching events.

count.description: Number of events returned (mode=query) or matched (mode=count).

query.description: The request's own query parameters, exactly as forwarded from the HTTP layer into the adapter.

retrieved_at_utc.description: ISO-8601 UTC time this route fetched the data.

url.description: The exact upstream request URL, including format=geojson and all forwarded params.

generated.description: ISO-8601 UTC time USGS generated the response (from GeoJSON metadata.generated).

enum: USGS data are in the public domain (https://www.usgs.gov/information-policies-and-instructions/copyrights-and-credits)

InvalidQueryError.description: server/serverless/earthquakes-route.js maps a validateQuery() failure (server/sources/usgs-earthquakes.js) to this shape; `unknown` is always present (possibly empty) and is what distinguishes this from UpstreamError.

message.description: Human-readable reason, e.g. "Invalid limit: expected an integer >= 1" or "circle (latitude/longitude/maxradiuskm) and bbox (...) are mutually exclusive".

unknown.description: Names of any query parameters not recognised by the adapter. Empty when the failure was a value/range/mutual-exclusivity error rather than an unknown key.

UpstreamError.description: Either the route's own unhandled-exception fallback (SourcesError) or a pass-through USGS/network failure (AdapterError). No `unknown` key -- that is what distinguishes this from InvalidQueryError.

SourcesError.description: server/serverless/earthquakes-route.js's outer catch-all: any unhandled exception in the handler.

AdapterError.description: server/sources/usgs-earthquakes.js requestUsgs(): a USGS-side or network-side failure passed through by the route as `{error, detail}`.

detail.description: Up to 200 characters of the upstream response body, or the underlying network/timeout error message.
